intro.heading: The hardest part of the whole process
intro.body: Italy's student housing supply doesn't cover demand, especially in the biggest academic cities. Private landlords often ask for guarantees — a local payslip, a domestic guarantor — that an international student simply doesn't have.

visaParadox.heading: The paradox: proof of address before you've even seen the place
visaParadox.body: Your visa application needs a valid address in Italy, but most landlords won't commit to a tenant they've never met, months in advance. This is the exact point where students without support get stuck — or get scammed.

scamWarning.heading: How rental scams usually work
scamWarning.body: Being forced to book before arrival makes students an easy target for listings that don't exist. Never send money without a contract you can actually verify.
warningSigns: The landlord refuses a video call or won't let anyone view the place in person
Pressure to pay a deposit within hours, before you've seen a contract
Requests to transfer money to an account abroad, outside normal channels
A price well below what similar rooms cost in that area

whatWeDo.heading: What we do
items: Review your contract before you sign anything
Handle lease registration — a legal requirement, and a precondition for your residency
Prepare a *dichiarazione di ospitalità* if you need proof of address before your lease is final
Point you toward verified student residences and checked listings
Support you in Italian where the paperwork requires it

whatWeDontDo.heading: What we don't do
items: We're not a licensed real estate agency, and we don't act as one
We don't hold listings or collect deposits on a landlord's behalf
We can't guarantee you a specific room, or that any given search will succeed

cities.range: Often €600–700+ per month for a single room
Typically €250–700 per month, depending on the type of accommodation

euSection.heading: If you're an EU student on Erasmus
euSection.body: You don't need a visa, so the proof-of-address requirement doesn't apply to you the same way — but the market is just as tight. Landlords often prefer long-term tenants over a 6–9 month Erasmus stay, so start your search early and expect the same scam patterns described above.
